# Mise en place

Before the heat goes on, everything is measured, cut and arranged within reach. I write a short checklist the evening before: which stations need which tools, what must be chopped first, what can wait. The order of operations matters more than speed. A dry run of the trickiest dish, even only in my head, shows where I would otherwise stop mid-service and hunt for a spoon.

The payoff of the preparation is calm. Interruptions during cooking are expensive, so the whole point is that nothing needs fetching once the pan is hot. Small bowls, labelled trays, one clean cloth per station. When I skip this step the evening always feels like firefighting, and the food suffers.

I keep the checklist as a plain list on paper and cross things out as they are done.
